module: Generic assembly of mesh "parts" for baked kit pieces (bridgeKit, islandKit, etc.). A part is { verts, normals, uvs, faces } where each entry of faces is { v, n, u } with 0-based indices, the format consumed by both ProceduralMesh and the DAE export. All kit geometry goes through here to share a single winding convention. Also provides ear clipping triangulation, chamfered posts and emitObject, which creates the ProceduralMesh in the scene.
usage:
local mp = require('editor/toolUtilities/meshPart')
local part = mp.newPart()
mp.face4(part, p1, p2, p3, p4, 0, 0, 1, {0,0}, {1,0}, {1,1}, {0,1}) -- face visible on the +Z side
mp.emitObject(folder, 'ma_dalle', {part}, false)
notes: Winding: the front face of a ProceduralMesh has its geometric winding normal pointing AWAY from the visible side; the stored shading normal points toward the visible side. The face* functions take a reference point (rx, ry, rz) = direction of the visible side and flip the winding if needed. Do not assemble faces by hand with the opposite convention (daeExport flips the winding only once).
The faces entries hold one record per triangle CORNER (three per triangle); face4 writes 6 corners, face3 writes 3.

Engine limit: ProceduralMesh fills a 16-bit index buffer with a 16-bit counter; beyond 65535 corners in a mesh, the counter overflows and the game freezes. emitObject therefore cuts at 60000 corners per mesh and then returns a SimGroup of several meshes.
The created meshes have canSave = false. Without collide, collisionType is 'None'. Parts coming from a pool are not kept for partsOf (they are reused).
UV: {u, v} lists; points are { x, y, z } tables.

newPool.desc: Creates a pool of reusable parts, for parts emitted then discarded again and again. The engine copies the mesh data on creation: a part passed through emitObject no longer needs to be kept.

poolReset.desc: Resets the pool counter to zero: the parts handed out again by newPart(pool) will be filled anew.

newPart.desc: Returns an empty part { verts, normals, uvs, faces }. With a pool, reuses the next part of the pool, emptying its tables (the inner entries are kept to avoid allocations).

face4.desc: Emits a quad p1 -> p2 -> p3 -> p4 into the part, with the front face visible on the side of the vector (rx, ry, rz). The shading normal is the face's (toward the visible side), unless snx/sny/snz is provided (the winding always follows the geometry).

face4n.desc: Like face4 but with one shading normal per corner (n1..n4 = {x, y, z}), to smoothly shade a bumpy surface from precomputed vertex normals instead of a single facet normal.

n1.desc: Normal of corner 1 {x, y, z}, toward the visible side.

face3.desc: Emits a triangle p1 -> p2 -> p3 with the same winding contract as face4. For flat caps (roofs, terraces) where a quad does not fit.

faces3.desc: Emits triangles on shared corners, all flat-shaded: corner i at (x[i], y[i], z[i]) with uv (u[i], v[i]), nv corners and nt triangles whose corners are tri[3t-2..3t] (1-based indices). Each triangle is wound like face3, but a corner is stored only once.

quad.desc: Emits a quad that may actually be a TRIANGLE (one corner coinciding with its neighbor within 1e-6): in that case calls face3 instead of wasting a zero-area triangle; otherwise calls face4.

ccwRing.desc: Returns the closed ring of {x, y} pairs wound counter-clockwise (the outward normal of an edge a->b is (dy, -dx)). If the ring is already counter-clockwise, it is returned as is; otherwise a reversed copy.

triangulate.desc: Ear clipping triangulation of a counter-clockwise ring. Stops without finishing if no ear is found (degenerate or self-intersecting ring).

returns.desc: Index triplets {i0, i1, i2} into poly.

postPlan.desc: Outline of a square post of half-width d centered at (cx, cy), vertical edges chamfered by cham (counter-clockwise). Below 0.1 mm of chamfer, it is the plain square (4 points); otherwise an octagon (8 points).

postStage.desc: One dressed post stage (pier die, post cap): the postPlan outline extruded from z0 to z1, all faces facing outward and both ends closed. UV in meters multiplied by uv (U around the outline, V along the height).

scaleUVs.desc: Scales in place the UVs of a list of parts: lets a kit lay out its UVs in meters and then convert to the kit's tiling at bake time.

tintParts.desc: Applies a tint to each part of the list whose material field equals m. Without tint, does nothing.

partsTris.desc: Number of triangles in a list of parts (faces entries divided by 3), to report what a bake actually wrote.

partsCentre.desc: Center of the extent of a list of parts. A shape is written around this point and its static object is placed there: written around the world origin, it would lose precision far out on the map. Returns 0, 0, 0 if the list is empty.

emitObject.desc: Builds a ProceduralMesh named name from parts, in folder, replacing any object of the same name (which survives a Lua-only reload). A nil name leaves the mesh unnamed. Beyond 60000 corners, returns a SimGroup of several meshes under that name instead. Without collision by default.

collide.desc: Bake a collision (where the mesh is the only surface, for example a curb the car must feel).

decalSurface.desc: Marks the mesh as a surface onto which decals apply.

partsOf.desc: Returns the parts from which a live mesh was built (by id), so it can later be exported as a shape. Nil for a mesh made from pool parts. The table is purged of vanished meshes every 2000 records.

markDecalSurface.desc: Marks an object as a decal-draped surface (deck, slab, tunnel floor, paved square) by setting decalSurface = '1' (saved with the object). Decals project onto static shapes but not onto Forest items: these objects therefore stay TSStatics.

isDecalSurface.desc: Tells whether an object is marked as a decal surface.
